content.intro: Print a Skip-Bo score sheet for playing to 500, or keep score on your phone. One hand is quick; a game to 500 takes an evening, and the sheet keeps track.
howToUse: Write each player's name at the top of a column. A hand ends when one player plays the last card from their stockpile. That player wins the hand and is the only one who scores.
The winner scores 25 points, plus 5 points for every card still in the other players' stockpiles. Count those cards, work out the total and write it in the winner's column; leave the others empty.
Keep playing hands until someone reaches 500 points. Online, the sheet adds every hand and shows the winner as soon as someone passes 500. For a shorter game, just play one hand and skip the scoring.

faqs.a: The player who empties their stockpile first wins the hand and scores 25 points, plus 5 points for each card left in their opponents' stockpiles. The other players score nothing that hand.

faqs.q: How many points do you need to win Skip-Bo?
faqs.a: 500. Players keep playing hands until someone's total reaches 500. Many families play a single hand instead, and the first to empty their stockpile wins.

faqs.q: How many cards are in each stockpile?
faqs.a: 30 cards each for two to four players, and 20 cards each for five or six players.
Skip-Bo cards are wild. They can be played as any number on a building pile.

faqs.q: What happens when a building pile reaches 12?
faqs.a: The completed pile is set aside and shuffled back into the draw pile when it runs out, and a new building pile can be started with a 1 or a Skip-Bo card.

faqs.q: How many people can play Skip-Bo?
faqs.a: Two to six players, or six in teams of two. The printable sheet and the online scorekeeper both have room for six.
